questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the AWS availability zones and edge locations?

options.text: Edge locations are located in separate Availability Zones worldwide to serve global customers.
An availability zone exists within an edge location to distribute content globally with low latency.
An Availability Zone is a geographic location where AWS provides multiple, physically separated and isolated edge locations.
An AWS Availability Zone is an isolated location within an AWS Region, however edge locations are located in multiple cities worldwide.

questions.explanation: An Availability Zone is an isolated location within an AWS Region, while Edge Locations are separate sites in many cities worldwide used for content delivery (CloudFront). AZs and edge locations are distinct concepts.

questions.question: Which features are included in the AWS Business Support Plan? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Access to Cloud Support Engineers via email only during business hours.
Access to the Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) feature for additional fee.
Partial access to the core Trusted Advisor checks.

questions.explanation: Business Support includes 24x7 access to customer service (A) and access to Infrastructure Event Management for an additional fee (C). Business gets the full Trusted Advisor set and 24/7 engineer access; email-only business-hours support is Developer, and a 24x7 TAM is Enterprise.

questions.question: A company is developing a mobile application and wants to allow users to use their Amazon, Apple, Facebook, or Google identities to authenticate to the application. Which AWS Service should the company use for this purpose?
questions.explanation: Amazon Cognito lets users sign in with social/identity providers like Amazon, Apple, Facebook, and Google. GuardDuty is threat detection, Personalize is ML recommendations, and IAM is for AWS account access.

questions.question: Which AWS Service allows customers to create a template that programmatically defines policies and configurations of all AWS resources as code and so that the same template can be reused among multiple projects?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation lets you define AWS resources and configurations as code in a reusable template that can be deployed across multiple projects/environments. Config, CloudTrail, and Auto Scaling do not provision resources from templates.

questions.question: Which of the following are advantages of using AWS as a cloud computing provider? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Eliminates the need to monitor servers and applications.
Manages all the compliance and auditing tasks.
Provides custom hardware to meet any specification.
Eliminates the need to guess on infrastructure capacity needs.
Enables customers to trade their capital expenses for operational expenses.

questions.explanation: AWS advantages include eliminating the need to guess capacity (D) (scale up/down on demand) and trading capital expenses for operating expenses (E). AWS does not remove all monitoring, handle all compliance for you, or build custom hardware to any spec.

questions.question: A customer is planning to migrate their Microsoft SQL Server databases to AWS. Which AWS Services can the customer use to run their Microsoft SQL Server database on AWS? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: You can run Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2 (B) (self-managed) or Amazon RDS (C) (managed). Fargate and Lambda are not for SQL Server, and DMS only migrates data.

questions.question: Which AWS Service can perform health checks on Amazon EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 can perform health checks on EC2 instances (and other endpoints) and route traffic away from unhealthy ones. CloudFormation, Chime, and Aurora do not perform EC2 health checks.

questions.question: A company is developing an application that will leverage facial recognition to automate photo tagging. Which AWS Service should the company use for facial recognition?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition provides image and video analysis, including facial recognition for automated photo tagging. Comprehend is NLP, Polly is text-to-speech, and IAM is access management.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of AWS-managed databases? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2.

questions.explanation: Amazon Neptune (A) and Amazon RDS for MySQL (E) are AWS-managed databases. Databases you install yourself on EC2 (MySQL, SQL Server) are self-managed, and CloudSearch is a search service.

questions.question: A company’s AWS workflow requires that it periodically perform large-scale image and video processing jobs. The customer is seeking to minimize cost and has stated that the amount of time it takes to process these jobs is not critical, but that cost minimization is the most important factor in designing the solution. Which EC2 instance class is best suited for this processing?
questions.explanation: For periodic, time-flexible batch image/video processing where cost is paramount, EC2 Spot Instances are the cheapest option. On-Demand and Reserved cost more for interruptible, non-urgent work.

questions.question: There is a requirement to grant a DevOps team full administrative access to all resources in an AWS account. Who can grant them these permissions?
questions.explanation: Only the AWS account owner (root or an admin they designate) can grant the DevOps team full administrative access. A TAM, the security team, and support engineers cannot grant permissions in your account.

questions.question: You need to migrate a large number of on-premises workloads to AWS. Which AWS service is the most appropriate?
questions.explanation: AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) is the primary lift-and-shift service for migrating large numbers of on-premises servers and workloads to AWS. It replaced the now-retired AWS Server Migration Service (SMS). AWS DMS migrates databases, and Application Discovery Service only inventories on-premises resources before a migration.

questions.question: What are some key benefits of using AWS CloudFormation? (Choose TWO)

options.text: It helps AWS customers deploy their applications without worrying about the underlying infrastructure.
It applies advanced IAM security features automatically.
It automates the provisioning and updating of your infrastructure in a safe and controlled manner.
It allows you to model your entire infrastructure in just a text file.
It compiles and builds application code in a timely manner.

questions.explanation: CloudFormation automates provisioning and updating of infrastructure in a safe, controlled manner (C) and lets you model your entire infrastructure in a text file/template (D). It does not auto-apply IAM features or build application code.

questions.question: Which of the following is a cloud computing deployment model that connects infrastructure and applications between cloud-based resources and existing resources not located in the cloud?
questions.explanation: A Hybrid deployment model connects cloud-based resources with existing on-premises (non-cloud) resources. On-premises and 'Cloud' are single-environment models, and 'Mixed' is not an AWS term.

questions.question: A company is hosting business critical workloads in an AWS Region. To protect against data loss and ensure business continuity, a mirror image of the current AWS environment should be created in another AWS Region. Company policy requires that the standby environment must be available in minutes in case of an outage in the primary AWS Region. Which AWS service can be used to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS DRS) continuously replicates your servers to another Region and lets you launch recovery within minutes, meeting a low-RTO disaster-recovery requirement. AWS DRS is the renamed successor to CloudEndure Disaster Recovery. AWS Backup protects data but does not provide minutes-fast standby failover.

questions.question: Which of the following S3 storage classes is most appropriate to host static assets for a popular e-commerce website with stable access patterns?
questions.explanation: For frequently accessed static assets with stable access patterns, S3 Standard is most appropriate (no retrieval fees, high availability). Standard-IA, Intelligent-Tiering, and Deep Archive suit infrequent or unpredictable access.

questions.question: You want to create a backup of your data in another geographical location. Where should you create this backup?
questions.explanation: To protect against geographic disaster, create the backup in another AWS Region. Another AZ is still in the same Region, an edge location is for caching, and a VPC is a virtual network.

questions.question: Which statement is true in relation to the security of Amazon EC2?

options.text: You should use instance store volumes to store login data.
You should regularly patch the operating system and applications on your EC2 instances.
You should deploy critical components of your application in the Availability Zone that you trust.
You can track all API calls using Amazon Athena.

questions.explanation: A key EC2 security practice is to regularly patch the guest operating system and applications, which is the customer's responsibility. Instance store is ephemeral (bad for login data), and API calls are tracked with CloudTrail, not Athena.

questions.question: What does AWS Cost Explorer provide to help manage your AWS spend?

options.text: Cost comparisons between AWS Cloud environments and on-premises environments.
Accurate estimates of AWS service costs based on your expected usage.
Highly accurate cost forecasts for up to 12 months ahead.

questions.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer can produce cost forecasts for up to 12 months ahead based on your historical usage. Estimates from expected usage come from the Pricing Calculator, and on-premises comparisons came from the TCO Calculator.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of Amazon RDS that performs automatic failover when the primary database fails to respond?
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ maintains a standby replica and performs automatic failover if the primary database becomes unavailable. Single-AZ has no failover, and 'Write Replica' is not an RDS feature.

questions.question: You are using several on-demand EC2 Instances to run your development environment. What is the best way to reduce your charges when these instances are not in use?

options.text: Deleting all EBS volumes attached to the instances.
You cannot minimize charges for on-demand instances.

questions.explanation: Stopping On-Demand EC2 instances when not in use halts compute charges (you keep the EBS data and can restart later). Terminating would delete the dev environment, and deleting EBS volumes loses data.

questions.question: Which of the following strategies helps protect your AWS root account?

options.text: Delete root user access keys if you do not need them.
Apply MFA for the root account and use it for all of your work.
Access the root account only from your personal Mobile Phone.
Only share your AWS account password or access keys with trusted persons.

questions.explanation: A key root-account protection is to delete the root user's access keys if you do not need them, reducing exposure. You should not use root for daily work or share account credentials.

questions.question: Which of the following are factors should be considered for Amazon EBS pricing? (Choose TWO)

options.text: The size of volumes provisioned per month.
The amount of data you have stored in snapshots.
The number of Snowball storage devices you request.

questions.explanation: EBS pricing depends on the size of volumes provisioned per month (A) and the amount of data stored in snapshots (C). Compute capacity/time is EC2, and Snowball devices are separate.

questions.question: You have just set up your AWS environment and have created six IAM user accounts for the DevOps team. What is the AWS recommendation when granting permissions to these IAM accounts?

options.text: Attach a separate IAM policy for each individual account.
Apply the Principle of Least Privilege.
For security purposes, you should not grant any permission to the DevOps team.

questions.explanation: When granting permissions to the IAM accounts, apply the Principle of Least Privilege — grant only what each user needs. The other options are insecure or impractical.

questions.question: Which of the following has the greatest impact on cost? (Choose TWO)

options.text: The number of IAM roles provisioned.

questions.explanation: Compute charges (A) and Data Transfer Out charges (D) typically have the greatest impact on the AWS bill. Data Transfer In is generally free, and IAM roles/number of services are not direct cost drivers.

questions.question: Who from the following will get the largest discount?

options.text: A user who chooses to buy On-demand, Convertible, Partial upfront instances.
A user who chooses to buy Reserved, Convertible, All upfront instances.
A user who chooses to buy Reserved, Standard, No upfront instances.
A user who chooses to buy Reserved, Standard, All upfront instances.

questions.explanation: The largest discount comes from a Reserved, Standard, All Upfront purchase — Standard RIs discount more than Convertible, and All Upfront discounts more than Partial/No Upfront. On-Demand offers no commitment discount.

questions.question: Which of the following is an available option when purchasing Amazon EC2 instances?

options.text: The ability to bid to get the lowest possible prices.
The ability to register EC2 instances to get volume discounts on every hour the instances are running.
The ability to buy Dedicated Instances for up to 90% discount.
The ability to pay upfront to get lower hourly costs.

questions.explanation: A real EC2 purchasing option is paying upfront (Reserved Instances) to get lower hourly costs. Spot no longer uses customer bidding, there is no per-hour 'volume registration,' and Dedicated Instances are not a flat 90% discount.

questions.question: What does the term “Economies of scale” mean?

options.text: It means that you save more when you consume more.
It means as more time passes using AWS, you pay more for its services.
It means that AWS will continuously lower costs as it grows.
It means that you have the ability to pay as you go.

questions.explanation: 'Economies of scale' means AWS's massive scale lets it continuously lower costs and pass savings to customers. It is not about paying more over time or simple pay-as-you-go.

questions.question: A company experiences fluctuations in traffic patterns to their e-commerce website when running flash sales. What service can help the company dynamically match the required compute capacity to handle spikes in traffic during flash sales?
questions.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling dynamically matches compute capacity to demand, handling traffic spikes during flash sales and scaling back afterward. EC2 alone, EFS, and ElastiCache do not auto-match capacity.

questions.question: Which of the below options is true of Amazon VPC?

options.text: Amazon VPC allows customers to control user interactions with all other AWS resources.
AWS Customers have complete control over their Amazon VPC virtual networking environment.
AWS is responsible for all the management and configuration details of Amazon VPC.
Amazon VPC helps customers to review their AWS architecture and adopt best practices.

questions.explanation: With Amazon VPC, customers have complete control over their virtual networking environment (IP ranges, subnets, route tables, gateways). VPC is not for user permissions, is not fully AWS-managed, and is not an architecture review tool.

questions.question: Which tool can a non-AWS customer use to compare the cost of on-premises environment resources to AWS?
questions.explanation: The AWS TCO Calculator let even non-AWS customers compare on-premises resource costs against AWS. (Note: AWS has since retired the standalone TCO Calculator in favor of the AWS Pricing Calculator.) Cost Explorer and Budgets require an existing AWS account.

questions.question: Which of the following services provide real-time auditing for compliance and vulnerabilities? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS Config (A) continuously evaluates resource configurations for compliance, and AWS Trusted Advisor (D) checks for security and best-practice issues in near real time. Redshift, MQ, and Cognito are not auditing tools.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services uses Puppet to automate how EC2 instances are configured?
questions.explanation: AWS OpsWorks offers managed Puppet (and Chef) to automate how EC2 instances are configured. CloudFormation provisions resources, Quick Starts are reference deployments, and CloudTrail logs API calls.

questions.question: An organization uses a hybrid cloud architecture to run their business. Which AWS service enables them to deploy their applications to any AWS or on-premises server?
questions.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy automates application deployments to Amazon EC2, on-premises servers, Lambda, and ECS, supporting hybrid architectures. Kinesis, QuickSight, and Athena do not deploy applications.

questions.question: Select the services that are server-based: (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS (A) and Amazon EMR (E) are server-based (they run on instances you size). DynamoDB, Lambda, and Fargate are serverless.

questions.question: What best describes penetration testing?

options.text: Testing your application’s response time from different locations.
Testing your network to find security vulnerabilities that an attacker could exploit.
Testing your instances to check for the unhealthy ones.
Testing your software for bugs and errors.

questions.explanation: Penetration testing means deliberately probing your network/application to find security vulnerabilities an attacker could exploit. It is not latency testing, health checking, or general bug testing.

questions.question: Which of the following are use cases for Amazon EMR? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Enables you to backup extremely large amounts of data at very low costs.
Enables you to move Exabyte-scale data from on-premises datacenters into AWS.
Enables you to analyze and process extremely large amounts of data in a timely manner.
Enables you to easily run and scale Apache Spark, Hadoop,and other Big Data frameworks.
Enables you to easily run and manage Docker containers.

questions.explanation: Amazon EMR lets you analyze and process extremely large datasets quickly (C) and easily run/scale frameworks like Apache Spark and Hadoop (D). Low-cost backup is Glacier, exabyte transfer is Snowmobile, and containers are ECS/EKS.

questions.question: Your CTO has asked you to contact AWS support using the chat feature to ask for guidance related to EBS. However, when you open the AWS support center you can't see a way to contact support via Chat. What should you do?

options.text: There is no chat feature in AWS support.
The chat feature is available for all plans for an additional fee, but you have to request it first.
At a minimum, upgrade to Business support plan.
Upgrade from the Basic Support plan to Developer Support.

questions.explanation: Chat (and phone) support requires at least the Business Support plan; the Basic and Developer plans do not include chat with engineers. So you must upgrade to at least Business.

questions.question: A developer wants to quickly deploy and manage his application in the AWS Cloud, but he doesn’t have any experience with cloud computing. Which of the following AWS services would help the developer achieve his goal?
questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk lets a developer with no cloud experience deploy and manage an application easily — it handles the underlying infrastructure automatically. Fargate, Batch, and Personalize do not provide this all-in-one app management.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the AWS Pay-As-You-Go pricing model?

options.text: With AWS, you replace low upfront expenses with large variable payments.
With AWS, you replace low upfront expenses with large fixed payments.
With AWS, you replace large upfront expenses with low fixed payments.
With AWS, you replace large capital expenses with low variable payments.

questions.explanation: AWS Pay-As-You-Go replaces large upfront capital expenses with low variable payments based on actual usage. The other phrasings misstate the model (no large fixed/variable upfront commitments).

questions.question: For Amazon RDS databases, what does AWS perform on your behalf? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: For Amazon RDS, AWS performs database setup/provisioning (A) and operating-system management/patching (C) on your behalf. You manage access, network protection configuration, and firewall (security group) rules.

questions.question: Which of the following strategies help analyze costs in AWS?

options.text: Using AWS CloudFormation to automate the deployment of resources.
Deploying resources of the same type in different regions.
Configuring Amazon Inspector to automatically analyze costs and email reports.

questions.explanation: Using tags to group resources lets you categorize and analyze costs (e.g., cost allocation tags by project or department). CloudFormation automates deployment, multi-Region duplication does not analyze cost, and Inspector is for security.

questions.question: A media company has an application that requires the transfer of large data sets to and from AWS every day. This data is business critical and should be transferred over a consistent connection. Which AWS service should the company use?
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated, consistent network connection for transferring large, business-critical data sets daily. Comprehend is NLP, Snowmobile is one-time physical transfer, and a VPN runs over the variable public internet.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of the AWS Storage Gateway service?

options.text: It automates the process of building, maintaining, and running ETL jobs.
It provides physical devices to migrate data from on premises to AWS.
It allows integration of on-premises IT environments with Cloud Storage.
It provides hardware-based key storage for regulatory compliance.

questions.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway integrates on-premises IT environments with AWS Cloud storage, providing low-latency local access backed by AWS. It is not an ETL tool, a physical-transfer device, or a hardware key store.

questions.question: To protect against data loss, you need to backup your database regularly. What is the most cost-effective storage option that provides immediate retrieval of your backups?
questions.explanation: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access is the most cost-effective option that still offers immediate retrieval for regularly needed database backups. Glacier and Deep Archive are cheaper but do not retrieve immediately, and Instance Store is ephemeral.

questions.question: Which service can you use to route traffic to the endpoint that provides the best application performance for your users worldwide?
questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator routes user traffic over the AWS global network to the endpoint that delivers the best performance worldwide. Data Pipeline, DAX, and 'Transfer Acceleration' serve other purposes.

questions.question: Why are Serverless Architectures more economical than Server-based Architectures?

options.text: Serverless Architectures use new powerful computing devices.
With the Server-based Architectures, compute resources continue to run all the time but with serverless architecture, compute resources are only used when code is being executed.
When you reserve serverless capacity, you will get large discounts compared to server reservation.
With Serverless Architectures you have the ability to scale automatically up or down as demand changes.

questions.explanation: Serverless architectures are more economical because compute is consumed only while code runs, whereas server-based architectures keep resources running (and billable) continuously. Auto-scaling is a benefit but not the core economic reason here.

questions.question: Which of the below options are use cases of the Amazon Route 53 service? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Point-to-point connectivity between an on-premises data center and AWS.
Detects configuration changes in the AWS environment.
Manages global application traffic through a variety of routing types.

questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 use cases include DNS configuration and management (C) and managing global application traffic with various routing policies (D). Point-to-point connectivity (Direct Connect), config-change detection (Config), and security recommendations (Trusted Advisor) are other services.

questions.question: You want to transfer 200 Terabytes of data from on-premises locations to the AWS Cloud, which of the following can do the job in a cost-effective way?
questions.explanation: For transferring 200 TB cost-effectively, AWS Snowball (physical device shipping) is appropriate. Snowmobile is for exabyte/petabyte-scale transfers, DMS migrates databases, and Import/Export is the retired predecessor.

questions.question: You have a real-time IoT application that requires sub-millisecond latency. Which of the following services should you use?
questions.explanation: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis delivers sub-millisecond in-memory latency suited to real-time IoT applications. Redshift (analytics), Athena (query), and Cloud9 (IDE) cannot meet sub-millisecond latency needs.
